Looks like a pretty bad source. I'd heard nothing about this and did some Googling. So far as I can tell it looks like this article is a rehash of this article with all the details, context, and interesting information removed.

And also no, there are no plans to colonize the moon in 6 years. The research the article was referencing (which some NASA scientists were part of) was certainly endorsing the idea of putting up a permanent 10 man base on the moon which would expand to a self sufficient 100 man base of the next decade, but going from that to "NASA and SpaceX to colonize moon in 7 years" is a more than a little stretch.

Considering we have Russia planning on establishing a colony on the moon by around 2027-2030, China making plans to do the same starting in the 20s some time (they may shoot astronauts around the moon as early as next year and test different technologies), the European Space Agency working on their own collaborative moon project, and even India talking about future moon plans, it seems likely that the United States would want to preemptively start working on something similar out of fear of being left behind in mining, living, and exploration technologies. And just this year, Johann-Dietrich Wörner, Chief of NASA ESA , propose a moon base as the successor for ISS, which gives it at least a little credibility.

I'm in the camp of believe it when I see it, and the article wasn't very good, but if Russia and China are on there way there, you can bet that the United States won't be left standing around with their pants around their ankles.
